skill.name: webask-quiz-from-brief
skill.description: Собирает готовый опрос в WebAsk по описанию задачи на обычном языке. Применяется, когда человек просит сделать опрос, анкету, форму заявки, тест или квиз и описывает словами, что нужно узнать и у кого, вместо перечисления конкретных вопросов.
skill.summary: Create WebAsk surveys from natural-language briefs, with suitable question types, conditional logic, themes, and publication after approval.
skill.author: webaskio

security_audit.summary: All 24 static findings are false positives: README navigation links and Markdown code spans, not path traversal or shell execution. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential theft, or unauthorized data transfer in the reviewed files. The workflow uses WebAsk MCP tools and requires publication approval; the external service implementation was not audited.

finding_verdicts.reason: The parent-directory sequences are fixed HTML breadcrumb links to repository documentation. They do not perform filesystem access or process attacker-controlled paths.
Backticks format MCP template-search and creation tool names in Markdown. The surrounding prose describes survey creation, not Ruby or shell execution.
The inline code spans name create_quiz and update_quiz_widgets as MCP operations. There is no shell interpreter or executable command substitution.
get_folder_list is a Markdown-formatted WebAsk tool name for choosing a survey folder. The following text requires clarification when multiple folders exist.
The table compares rating and input question types using Markdown code spans. These are widget identifiers, not executable shell expressions.
The backticks identify the nps widget in a question-selection table. No command execution is described or embedded.
The table contrasts dropdown and input widgets for selecting one option. Backticks provide Markdown formatting only.
The inline dropdown identifier describes a multiple-selection question type. It is documentation rather than a shell command.
The fio identifier denotes a name-entry widget in a Markdown table. No interpreter evaluates the backticked text.
phone and email are documented survey field types with format validation. Their Markdown delimiters do not invoke external commands.
datetime is a question-type identifier for date and time responses. The line contains documentation, not shell or Ruby code.
matrix names a widget for collecting several related ratings. Backticks only distinguish the identifier within a Markdown table.
file denotes a respondent upload widget, not the operating-system file command. The table does not instruct shell execution or local file collection.
number is a Markdown-formatted numeric question type. There is no executable expression or command context.
yesno identifies a binary-response survey widget. The backticks are inline documentation markup, not command substitution.
ranking names the question type used to order choices. This table entry contains no shell execution instruction.
welcome and finish are survey screen identifiers in Markdown code spans. The prose specifies survey structure rather than executable commands.
The backticked text is a relative path to the bundled widget reference. It directs documentation reading without invoking a shell.
update_quiz_texts names the MCP operation for survey labels and messages. Markdown formatting does not make this shell execution.
get_theme_list and apply_quiz_theme are documented MCP operations for survey styling. No Ruby or shell evaluation appears.
update_quiz_logic names a tool for configuring conditional survey questions. The surrounding examples describe respondent routing, not operating-system commands.
get_quiz_structure is a Markdown-formatted MCP tool name. The instruction requires reading question identifiers before changing branching logic, with no shell execution.
publish_quiz names a WebAsk publishing operation, not a shell command. The same line explicitly requires user consent before publication.
generate_ai_quiz is an MCP tool identifier formatted as inline code. The following lines describe waiting for background survey generation, not running shell commands.

content.user_title: Create WebAsk Surveys from a Brief
content.value_statement: Turning a survey brief into suitable questions, branching, and formatting takes manual work. This skill guides connected WebAsk tools to create a draft and publish it after your approval.
actual_capabilities: Clarifies the audience, decision goal, and link placement, then searches for a suitable survey template.
Creates surveys in a selected WebAsk folder and chooses appropriate question types, including ratings, NPS, contact fields, and matrices.
Adds welcome and finish screens, audience-language text, and an existing account theme.
Reads question identifiers before configuring conditional branches and skip logic.
Requires approval before publishing and then reports the link, question count, required fields, and branching.
Uses background AI survey generation for long briefs and waits for completion before reviewing the result.
limitations: Requires access to a WebAsk account and the declared MCP tools; it is not a standalone survey application.
Account survey limits can prevent creation; the workflow stops rather than recommending a plan change.
Unpublished surveys are not accessible through the public response link, and publication requires explicit approval.
Booking and payment questions require an existing schedule or merchant account configured in WebAsk.

use_cases.title: Collect Service Feedback
use_cases.description: Create a short satisfaction survey with ratings, conditional follow-up questions, and contact fields for repeat bookings.

use_cases.title: Build Consultation Request Forms
use_cases.description: Turn a consultation brief into a form with name, phone, preferred time, and a question field.

use_cases.title: Prepare Product Research Surveys
use_cases.description: Create recommendation and feature-feedback questions, with branches that skip irrelevant sections for people who have not used the product.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Survey
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short WebAsk survey for recent delivery customers. Measure satisfaction and collect a phone number for follow-up. Show the draft before publishing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: turn a simple goal into a survey draft.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Consultation Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a consultation request form in [folder] for [audience]. Include name, phone, preferred time, and the client question. Use [language] and an existing theme. Ask me before publishing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: specify fields, location, and audience language.

prompt_templates.title: Add Conditional Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a service feedback survey for [audience] in [folder]. Ask for a rating and show a comment question only below four stars. Skip service ratings for nonusers. Read the structure before setting branches, and show the draft for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: configure branching using actual question identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Process a Detailed Research Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a WebAsk survey from this brief: [brief]. Use [folder] and [audience language]. Propose a matching template first. Use background generation if appropriate, wait for completion, and review the questions and branches. Keep it unpublished until I approve.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate template selection, background generation, and review.

output_examples.input: Draft a service feedback survey with a five-star rating, a comment below four stars, and a required callback phone number.
output: Example draft summary: three questions, plus welcome and finish screens.
Questions: service rating, conditional improvement comment, and callback phone number.
Branch: show the comment question for ratings below four stars.

output_examples.input: Create a consultation form with name, required phone, preferred time, and the client question. Keep it unpublished.
output: Example draft summary: four questions, plus welcome and finish screens.
Fields: name, validated phone number, date and time, and a text question.

best_practices: State the audience, decision goal, and link placement so questions stay focused.
Choose the destination folder and review required contact fields before approving the draft.
Test conditional routes and review audience-language text before explicitly approving publication.
anti_patterns: Requesting publication before reviewing the survey and its conditional routes.
Using free-text fields for ratings, contact details, or fixed-choice answers.
Adding unrelated questions or marking every field as required.

faq.question: Does this create a real survey or only suggest questions?
faq.answer: With connected WebAsk MCP tools, it creates and edits an actual survey. Without those tools, it cannot complete the creation workflow.

faq.question: Will it publish my survey automatically?
faq.answer: No. The workflow requires your approval before publishing. A public response link becomes usable after publication.

faq.question: Can it use existing templates and themes?
faq.answer: Yes. It searches for a matching template, leaves that choice to you, and can apply an existing account theme.

faq.question: Can it create conditional questions?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads the survey structure before configuring branches, such as showing a follow-up question after a low rating.

faq.question: Which language will the survey use?
faq.answer: The assistant replies in your language and writes survey text in the audience language. Specify that language when the two differ.

faq.question: What happens with long briefs or account limits?
faq.answer: Long briefs can use background generation, followed by review when complete. If survey limits block creation, the workflow explains the limit and stops.
